A frightened injured community cat is hiding under a parked car in Panaji, Goa. How can I move her safely, and where can she get treatment?

It is good that you are trying to help her. **First make sure nobody starts or moves the parked car.** Ask the driver to wait, keep the area quiet, and keep children/dogs back.

**To move her safely**
- Do **not** reach under the car or try to pull/grab her; a frightened injured cat may bite or run into traffic.
- Place an open, secure carrier on its side near her hiding place, with a little food at the far end only if she is alert and able to move. Step back and give her quiet time to enter voluntarily.
- If she will not come out, do not chase her. A local vet/rescue may be able to advise on a humane trap or safe collection. Towel handling is only suitable if she is calm enough not to struggle.
- If she has bleeding and comes within safe reach, apply gentle continuous pressure with a clean cloth. Do not put turmeric, oil, powders, or medicines on the wound.

A puppy was hit by a bike near Lalpur, Ranchi. What should I do first, and which nearby hospital treats animals?

A puppy hit by a bike may have internal injuries even if there is little visible blood, so please arrange veterinary assessment **now**.

- Move the puppy out of traffic only if you can do it safely. Keep them warm, quiet and as still as possible.  
- Do not try to straighten a leg, give medicines, food or water, or press on the belly.  
- If there is external bleeding, apply **gentle, continuous pressure with a clean cloth** if the puppy allows it. Use a box, carrier, or a flat board/blanket as a stretcher and support the whole body during transport.

Dogs chase my scooter on my evening ride in Lucknow. Would carrying a stick and waving it at them help?

I understand that can feel unsafe. **Carrying and waving a stick is not a good idea**—dogs may read it as a threat, which can make them more excited or defensive.

While riding, put **traffic safety first**: keep your line and speed predictable, look ahead, and avoid sudden braking, swerving, shouting, or gesturing at the dogs. If you can do so safely, plan a different route or ride at a time when that stretch is quieter.

If dogs repeatedly chase riders at one spot, note the exact lane/landmark and report it to the local municipal/Animal Husbandry service for a humane assessment. The issue may involve road traffic, territorial behaviour, or puppies nearby; feeding or waving objects is not a reliable fix.
I am scared to stop because they may bite. What can I do while riding?

Your fear makes sense—please **do not stop in moving traffic just because dogs are following**.

While riding:
- Keep your scooter steady and your attention on the road; avoid sudden braking, swerving, racing away, shouting, or waving at them.
- Keep both hands on the handlebars and continue toward a **safe, open, well-lit place** where you can pull over normally—such as a petrol pump, shop frontage, or a place with people—only when traffic conditions allow.
- Once safely stopped and off the traffic flow, keep the scooter between you and the dogs, stay calm, and wait for them to lose interest before moving on.
- For future trips, choose a different route around that particular stretch where possible. Repeated chasing can be linked to territory, puppies, or fast-moving vehicles; it does not mean every dog will bite.

If a dog ever bites or scratches you, wash the area immediately with soap and running water for at least **15 minutes** and get prompt medical care for rabies prevention.
